questions.q: Why does MariaDB's dialect transfer so closely from what you learn about MySQL?
options: MariaDB was forked from MySQL and shares almost all of its dialect
MariaDB and MySQL are unrelated products that happen to share a name pattern
MariaDB only supports standard ANSI SQL with no extensions
MySQL was forked from MariaDB, not the other way around
questions.explain: MariaDB forked from MySQL, inheriting nearly all of its SQL dialect.

questions.q: Which platform's dialect is noted for leaning Postgres-flavored, and why?
options: Amazon Redshift, because it was originally forked from PostgreSQL
Snowflake, because it was built directly on top of PostgreSQL's source code
BigQuery, because Google acquired PostgreSQL's parent company
Databricks, because Spark SQL is a renamed version of PostgreSQL
questions.explain: Redshift was originally forked from PostgreSQL, which is why its SQL dialect leans noticeably Postgres-flavored.

The name of PostgreSQL's query optimizer

questions.q: What distinguishes cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift) as a group from the four traditional relational platforms in this course?
options: They're built for analytics-at-scale (OLAP-style) workloads rather than traditional transactional (OLTP) workloads
They don't support SQL at all, only proprietary query languages
They are all owned and operated by the same company
They were all created before SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL existed
questions.explain: Cloud warehouses are purpose-built for analytics at scale, unlike the OLTP-oriented traditional relational platforms.
